newsitem.title: GERMANY: Tarkett - merger may involve plant closures.
newsitem.headline: Tarkett - merger may involve plant closures.

text.p: The merged floor coverings group Tarkett-Sommer AG may close some of its 27 plants worldwide to realise synergy benefits, Tarkett's chief executive Lars Wisen said on Wednesday.
"We estimate our capacity utilisation in Europe to be around 75 percent so we can squeeze more volume in fewer plants," Wisen told a presentation after the two companies announced the merger.

Asked if the company had concrete plans for plant closures and job cuts, Wisen said: "We have no firm plans on plant closures, of course I've got my ideas but will leave that to the management board to discuss and execute."
Wisen was speaking after Germany's Tarkett AG and French plastics group Sommer-Allibert announced earlier on Wednesday they were merging their floor covering businesses to create Tarkett-Sommer AG.
He said the move gave good opportunities to realise synergy benefits and limit investment in the coming years.

"We won't have so many manufacturers to invest in in future," Wisen said. Wisen added that Tarkett-Sommer was setting aside 20-25 million marks this year in provisions for restructuring, most of which will be spent in 1998.
Tarkett-Sommer will have 8,800 employees and 19 plants in Europe. Wisen, who will also be chief executive of the merged company, said there would also be "substantial restructuring" in the U.S.
